report.body:
Police in Água Clara, in Mato Grosso do Sul, arrested five men in an operation
against drug trafficking on the night of Wednesday 4 November 2026. Four of
them were booked in flagrante for drug trafficking and association for drug
trafficking, and the fifth was arrested on an existing court warrant. The
operation began after an anonymous tip that a man was selling drugs from a white
Volkswagen Gol in the Jardim das Palmeiras neighbourhood. Military Police
officers found the car, and after the driver fled and was chased for several
blocks he was stopped. The first suspect, aged 30, was already under
investigation by the Civil Police's General Investigations Section (SIG).

Officers found a portion of cocaine in the car and, at the driver's home,
portions of marijuana, a precision scale, packaging material and money. A
joint Military and Civil Police task force then found two more men at a snack
bar. At a second address used to store drugs, investigators found 59
tablets of marijuana weighing about 54 kg. Two men aged 18 and 20 were
arrested in flagrante at that address. Police also seized a car, a
motorcycle, three precision scales, three mobile phones, packaging and about
R$250 in cash.

The men were taken to the Civil Police station in Água Clara for legal
procedures. Police said the seizure should help the investigation into the
group's drug trade in the region.

2026 for holding hashish for sale and carrying a scalpel without legal
justification. The court also ordered them to pay costs and confiscated the
seized items. The verdict was issued by a bench headed by Judge Hamdi Abdel
Aziz, with judges Mohie Abu Kreisha and Amr Makki, and court secretaries Taha
Hussein and Maged Amin.

The three were convicted over 280 pieces of hashish seized in the case. A
chemical laboratory report found the seized material was brown hashish in three
lots of 80, 150 and 50 pieces, 280 in total, and a plastic sack bearing traces
of the drug. Drug control officers from the General Administration for Drug
Control's Middle Upper Egypt sector, Sohag branch, arrested them under a
prosecution warrant to search the first defendant. Prosecutors also accused
them of using cars to move and sell the hashish.

The charges date to November 2025, when investigators accused the three of
holding drugs for sale and promotion in Al-Maragha district in Sohag
Governorate. The defendants were aged 35, 25 and 41. All three were
from Al-Ghanaem district in Asyut Governorate, according to the committal order. The court had referred their papers to the Grand Mufti for a religious
opinion on executing them before delivering the verdict. After the Mufti's
opinion arrived the case returned to the court, which issued a final death
sentence reached by the unanimous opinion of the bench.

report.body:
Mossos d'Esquadra officers arrested seven men aged between 29 and 55 in an
industrial warehouse in Cabanes, Alt Empordà, on 1 October 2026. Inside the
warehouse, officers found the seven men unloading pallets from a trailer,
intending to load the hashish into vans for distribution. Four of the seven
were sent to prison provisionally without bail and three with bail, according to
ElCaso.cat. All seven were brought before the civil and investigation
section of the court in Figueres.

Officers seized 8,025 kg of hashish from the warehouse. The hashish was
hidden among legal merchandise in the trailer, inside large raffia sacks filled
with rubber shreds to defeat police and customs checks. The Mossos valued
the hashish at more than 16.2 million euros on the illegal market. Officers
also found a firearm in one of the detainees' vans. The seizure was a large
part of the roughly 14,900 kg of hashish the Mossos had seized in 2026 up to 1
October.

The investigation began in June 2026, when Mossos officers stopped a van
carrying nearly 2,400 kg of hashish in Viladecans, in the Baix Llobregat.
The criminal investigation section of the Gavà court took charge of the case. Surveillance of the warehouse showed people and vehicles arriving from time
to time with no business activity visible. Before the raid, officers saw
people swapping the number plates on the vehicles, apparently to hinder
identification. The investigation remains open and further arrests have not
been ruled out.

report.summary: Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta after finding a hidden compartment packed with bags of hashish, and on 15 November a judge ordered him held in preventive prison. Outlets estimate the haul at about 300 kilograms, pending an official weighing.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure. Officers used hammers, shears, sledgehammers and an angle grinder to break open the metal sheet covering the hidden compartment.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. A judge ordered the driver held in preventive prison on Sunday 15 November after he was brought before the court on an offence against public health.

report.title: Five arrested in Palma with 60 kg of hashish and weapons
report.summary: The National Police arrested four men and one woman in Palma after a parcel with 24 kilos of hashish led officers to two homes where they found another 36 kilos, 60 kilos in all. The searches also turned up two kilos of cocaine, about 10,000 euros in cash, an air rifle with a silencer and a pistol, and police said the investigation remains open.
report.body:
Officers of the National Police's Drugs and Organised Crime Unit (Udyco)
arrested at least three people on Mallorca who were storing almost 50 kilos of
hashish for sale. The five are four men and one woman, accused of drug trafficking and membership of a criminal group. The National Police said the investigation, which began months earlier, had ended with five people detained. The suspects received the hashish from the Spanish
mainland in courier parcels, according to the newspaper's case sources. Officers intercepted a parcel addressed to a man living in Palma that contained 24 kilos of hashish, and arrested him. The
arrests took place on Wednesday 4 November. Officers searched a home in
Marratxí, a municipality east of Palma, and another in a town in es Raiguer, the
district around the town of Inca. An investigating court in Palma declared
the case secret. Investigators had followed the suspects for some time;
over the previous months they had collected parcels of the drug from courier
companies and kept them at home for sale through others in the network.

In the Marratxí search, police found a large quantity of hashish in a chest
freezer and an air rifle. At the main suspect's home they found 36 kilos of hashish, an air rifle with a silencer and about 10,000 euros in cash, and arrested the man and a woman there. A woman was arrested there over her alleged link
to the criminal organisation and was released at the police station hours later. Two more people were arrested the same day, and all the suspects are
Spanish nationals. In total the operation seized 60 kilos of hashish. A fifth person was arrested for a link to the case. At the second home officers found two kilos of cocaine, a pistol with 9 mm cartridges, a bow with arrows and a hydraulic press, and arrested a suspect who police said stored and transported drugs.

The investigation is still open, further arrests are not ruled out, and the
suspects were due to appear before a Palma court in the coming hours.

customs administration said the Aragnouet tunnel, like the central Pyrenees, was

protecting citizens and residents from the scourge of drugs and to imposing the
strictest penalties prescribed by law on traffickers and dealers. It warned
that anyone who commits such offences would face the prescribed legal
punishment.

report.body:
Immigration police and officials of the Department of Thai Traditional and
Alternative Medicine searched a rented three-storey house on Soi Khu Bon 27 in
Tha Raeng, Bang Khen district, Bangkok, on 19 October 2026. They arrested a
Vietnamese man and four Myanmar workers who were sorting cannabis buds into bags
for delivery to customers. Black bags of cannabis buds were hidden across
all three floors of the house. Police said the buds weighed more than five
tonnes. The search was carried out under a warrant from the Min Buri
Criminal Court.

The raid followed complaints from neighbours about a strong cannabis smell that
had lasted for weeks. Officers spent about two months gathering evidence
before the search, the Immigration Bureau said. The house had an exhaust
pipe system built to discharge the smell outside. A Thai national had
signed the lease for the house. The foreigners had lived and worked at the
house for more than a year. The four Myanmar workers were paid 200 to 300
baht a day. Police suspect the Vietnamese man was managing the daily
operation.

An official of the Department of Thai Traditional and Alternative Medicine said
the operators held a licence valid only for Nong Bua Lamphu province, not
Bangkok. The business in Bangkok was illegal and carried a maximum penalty
of a year in prison and/or a 20,000 baht fine. Police sent the seized
cannabis to a laboratory to establish whether it was grown in Thailand or
imported. Investigators were also tracing the Thai tenant, the source of
the cannabis and any financiers.

growing cannabis. His brother paid the 133,120 hryvnias bail, which is to

report.body:
Saratoga County sheriff's deputies arrested Kevin C. Wilbur, 46, of Brushton,
and Quinton L. Carle, 23, of Bombay, after a traffic stop on the Northway in
Clifton Park. Deputies stopped a vehicle at 2:28 p.m. for following too
closely and insufficient tail lamps. Both men were charged with felony
first-degree criminal possession of cannabis. Wilbur was also cited for
following too closely and for having insufficient tail lamps.

Deputies seized 489 pounds (about 222 kilograms) of cannabis in the stop.
Wilbur and Carle are accused of knowingly and unlawfully possessing the 489
pounds of cannabis. Sheriff Jeffrey R. Brown said his deputies had
single-handedly prevented nearly a quarter ton of illicit cannabis from reaching
the streets.

Both men were arraigned before Judge Jennifer Jeram in Clifton Park Town Court. Wilbur was remanded to the Saratoga County Jail and Carle was released on

Kern County Sheriff's Office deputies arrested Rogelio Lorenzo Francisca, a
32-year-old man from Guerrero, Mexico, during a marijuana search in Taft,

arrest. The sheriff's office said he was held on suspicion of cultivating
marijuana, possessing marijuana for sale, conspiracy, and delaying, resisting or
obstructing an arrest.

October 2026 in the 27000 block of Highway 119 in Taft. They were assisted
by the sheriff's office High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas Task Force
(KC-HIDTA) and the Taft Police Department. The sheriff's office said the
deputies eradicated a total of 660 marijuana plants during the search.
Dangerous pesticides were also found within the grow site, the sheriff's office
said.

The sheriff's office said the investigation was active and ongoing. It
asked anyone with information about the case to contact the Kern County
Sheriff's Office or Kern Secret Witness.

attempts.decision_title: Cannabis legalisation in South Africa is CFI history
attempts.explanation: The Al Jazeera feature reports a change in the law, not an enforcement event: President Cyril Ramaphosa signed the Cannabis for Private Purposes Act the day before the 27 May 2024 general election, removing cannabis from South Africa's list of outlawed narcotics so that adults may grow and use it privately, while sale stays illegal outside prescribed medicinal use. It also recounts the 2018 Constitutional Court privacy ruling that forced the legislation and the roughly 3,000 people still in prison for cannabis offences as of 2022. Law changes, landmark rulings and national figures belong to the Cannabis Freedom Index history, so the submission is routed there rather than drafted as a tracker report. Enforcement appears only in passing, with no date, place, quantity or outcome: a 2020 raid on The Haze Club in Johannesburg with proceedings continuing, police helicopters spraying Eastern Cape dagga fields with herbicide, and a 2023 police instruction to stop making pot busts. A source reporting the Haze Club raid itself, or a specific spraying or seizure operation, would support a separate tracker report. The page's four photographs show the 2022 Cannabis Expo in Johannesburg and a cannabis grower in Eswatini, not an enforcement action, so none is listed as media.
